chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Tatum could not accompany singers; Tatum at the Embers
summary: Tatum overwhelmed Billie Holiday and the audience at the Embers; Horowitz said he wished he had Tatum's technique.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You know, he made some records with Joe Turner, the Blues things, and it seems as though those runs of his, he couldn't... I mean, they seem to be really very out of place there. They sound as though they were almost out of control.

Well, he couldn't accompany a singer, I wouldn't say, because he couldn't subjugate himself to that. He himself used to sing like the way he plays, you know. He played for Billie Holiday, and poor Billie, you know; you just had so much piano being played, Billie couldn't... It's difficult for a person like that to...

But Jonah Jones said when he was in L.A. they used to go out together, and after... He'd have Jonah sit down and play the Blues, and then he'd sit down and he'd play the Blues. And he loved to play them, and he used to be terrific! But we haven't got much of that on record.

No. Because his records were just... His horizon of music was so vast. I would say...especially... When he played anything, I mean, I could feel the embarrassment of the audience, especially at the Embers when he used to play there. The piano was right, a concert piano, and the way the man played... You could feel the
embarrassment of the audience. They'd feel, "We shouldn't be here; we should be at Carnegie Hall."
Yes. It's a bit out of place in a mere supper club.
Yeah. It was Jazz, but it was so profound...
Well, it's almost a sort of genre all its own. Because in a sense, you could say some of it was like super cocktail piano, wasn't it.
I mean, it wasn't all played with a strong beat or anything like that.

But you know? The thing is, it was Jazz, too. He played Jazz. He'd stride and he did everything. But it was just so much more, just like... I don't know. It was just... He was accenting. The accent, the whole presentation of the technique and everything was so profound that it just couldn't... Now, when he ran an arpeggio, it's just not running an arpeggio. That's an unusual type of an arpeggio. Like Horowitz once said, he said, "I wish I had his technique."
It was just an amazing thing. His hands were strong, his fingers were strong.
